column1: # Menu bar apps: casks this module installs that do nothing whatsoever until
# they are opened once. A launcher nobody launched has no hotkey, and a menu
# bar monitor that never ran has no menu bar item -- while `brew bundle` and
# the orphan scan both report a machine in perfect health, because the cask is
# on disk exactly as asked.
# Only apps that are USELESS until running belong here. Chrome, VS Code and
# Spotify are opened when you want them and are not this module's business.
# app name (the bundle under /Applications), the Brewfile cask that installs
# it, the preferences domain macOS creates on first launch, what you lose.
# Tab-separated, one app per line.
# Column 4 completes "installed but never opened -- no ...", so it starts with
# no article: doctor.sh owns the sentence and this file owns the words, and
# "no the launcher" is what having both own half of it reads like.
# tests/apps.bats holds every row to that.
# Column 2 is checked against Brewfile by tests/contract.bats: a row here is a
# claim that THIS module installs the app. Dropping the cask silences the row,
# which is the escape hatch for an app you decided you did not want.
Raycast
